Fetch the bytes of a plan

Source: R/fetch.R
zaro_fetch.Rd

Executes a zaro_plan(): returns the raw (still encoded) bytes of every chunk, in plan order, NULL for chunks that are absent (they read as fill_value). HTTP references are fetched concurrently through one curl connection pool with a per-host cap, adjacent byte ranges are merged into single requests, and failures are retried. zaro_read() and zaro_array() read through this, so they get the same batching.

Usage

zaro_fetch(
  store,
  plan,
  max_con = getOption("zaro.max_con", 8L),
  merge_gap = getOption("zaro.merge_gap", 0),
  retries = 2L,
  verbose = zaro_verbose()
)

Arguments

store

the store the plan was made from.

plan

a zaro_plan (or any refs table with the same columns).

max_con

integer. Maximum simultaneous HTTP connections, per host and in total. Default getOption("zaro.max_con", 8L).

merge_gap

numeric. Merge byte ranges on the same URL separated by at most this many bytes (the gap is fetched and discarded). Default getOption("zaro.merge_gap", 0): merge only touching ranges.

retries

integer. Retries for failed HTTP requests.

verbose

logical. Emit diagnostic messages. Default getOption("zaro.verbose", TRUE).

Value

A list of raw vectors (or NULL), one per plan row, with attribute "stats": HTTP requests, bytes received and seconds.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- zaro_plan(store, "temp", start = c(0, 0, 0, 0), count = c(1, 1, NA, NA))
raw <- zaro_fetch(store, p)
attr(raw, "stats")
} # }
